context_regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Advanced ovarian carcinoma that is refractory to platinum. This use of IV vinorelbine is unlicensed in Ireland.
context_regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Vinorelbine is being offered to slow the growth of platinum-refractory advanced ovarian cancer. Your team will review symptoms and scan results with you to decide whether to continue. IV vinorelbine on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle. Week three is a break. Your team reviews benefit and tolerability before repeating the cycle.
context_regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Vinorelbine disrupts the tiny structures a cell needs to divide. This can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy blood-forming cells, gut cells and nerves can also be affected.
context_regimen_profiles.schedule_context: NCCP days 1 and 8: vinorelbine 30 mg/m² IV over 15 minutes every 21 days. Flush the line with 250 mL sodium chloride 0.9% afterwards. Where marrow reserve is poor, the source describes a lower starting dose.
key_points: Before each cycle: blood count, kidney and liver tests and neuropathy review. The day-8 dose depends on blood counts and how you are feeling.
Call immediately for fever, chills or feeling suddenly unwell. During the infusion, report any pain or leakage around the IV line straight away.

context_regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Metastatic ovarian, fallopian tube or peritoneal carcinoma after earlier treatment has failed. The fallopian tube and peritoneal indications are unlicensed in Ireland.
context_regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Topotecan is being offered to slow the growth of metastatic ovarian, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer. Your team will review symptoms and scan results with you to decide whether to continue. A 30-minute infusion on each of five consecutive days, then a break through day 21. The standard plan is up to six cycles, stopping earlier for progression or unacceptable toxicity.
context_regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Metastatic ovarian, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer
context_regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Topotecan blocks topoisomerase I, an enzyme that relieves strain while DNA is copied. Unrepaired DNA breaks can stop dividing cancer cells; healthy blood-forming and gut cells can also be affected.
context_regimen_profiles.schedule_context: NCCP days 1–5: topotecan 1.5 mg/m² IV over 30 minutes every 21 days. The consultant may shorten the course to three or four days for toxicity or extensive pretreatment.
key_points: Repeat blood count and kidney and liver tests before each cycle. Low neutrophils, platelets or haemoglobin may require delay, dose change or supportive treatment.
Call immediately for fever, chills, sudden illness, uncontrolled bleeding or severe abdominal pain. New cough or breathlessness needs prompt assessment.
